title: Pacariqtambo, Puma Orco and Maukallaqta
summary: In Inca tradition the first Inca, Manco Capac, and his siblings emerged from a cave at Tambotoco. Brian Bauer proposed that the Puma Orco rock outcrop in Pacariqtambo district is that place, and that the nearby Inca ruins of Maukallaqta may have held an oracle of Manco Capac, built by Cuzco's elite to honor their legendary ancestor.

uncertainty.note: The opened pages do not date the ruins; Inca-period dating is approximate. The origin myth is recorded in Spanish chronicles written 1553-1613 and is a belief, not a dated event. EBSCO gives Manco Capac a mythohistorical reign of c. 1200-1230 and says the group left Pacaritambo early in the 13th century; the ruins themselves are Inca-period.

where.modern_name: Maukallaqta, Paccaritambo District, Paruro Province, Cusco Region, Peru (Puma Orco lies just to the east)
where.historical_name: Pacariqtambo, in the Inca heartland south of Cuzco, Tawantinsuyu

importance.justification: The place the Inca claimed as their origin; its link to the myth is a scholarly proposal.

sources.title: Pacariqtambo and the Mythical Origins of the Inca
sources.author: Brian S. Bauer

reviewer_note: The emergence from Tambotoco is an Inca origin myth, recorded as belief; only the sites and Bauer's identification are treated as factual. Inca-period dates (1400-1532) are approximate and not on an opened page. Only Bauer's abstract was read. The pin is Maukallaqta; Puma Orco's own coordinates were not found. EBSCO Research Starters added as the second source; its c. 1200-1230 date is for the legendary figure, not the buildings.
